services.description: Edu-Futuro is a nonprofit organization that empowers immigrant and underserved families through education, leadership development, and workforce readiness. The organization provides a wide range of programs and services designed to promote self-sufficiency and economic stability, including: Case Management and Emergency Assistance: Support for families experiencing housing instability, food insecurity, or financial crises through direct assistance, referrals, and resource navigation. Youth Programs: Leadership and college readiness programs (LEAD) for middle and high school students to prepare them for higher education and career success. Parent Empowerment Services: Workshops and coaching to help parents build advocacy, communication, and financial literacy skills. Workforce Development: Job readiness training, digital literacy, resume assistance, and connections to employment opportunities. Community Outreach and Referrals: Partnerships with local agencies, schools, and service providers to ensure holistic family support. Through these services, Edu-Futuro helps families achieve long-term stability and greater opportunities for success.

ACTS also runs a Rapid Re-Housing Program using a Housing First approach, and an Affordable Housing Program offering reduced rent in privately owned market-rate units for qualified low- and moderate-income households.

records.notes: Appointment required for all utility assistance; book at actspwc.org/schedule-an-appointment or by email to EAinfo@actspwc.org. No confirmation call or email is sent - the slot you select is your appointment. Applicants must be Prince William Area residents with a disconnection, eviction or foreclosure notice, and must have 30 uninterrupted minutes for an in-person interview. Utility assistance is limited to once every 6 months, and requesting an appointment does not guarantee payment. Translation services available.

services.description: The Emergency Assistance Program helps households in crisis facing disconnection of power or water, with benefits paid directly to the utility provider. Covers customers of NOVEC, Prince William County Service Authority, Columbia Gas, Virginia American Water, Dominion Energy, and City of Manassas and Manassas Park Utilities. ACTS is a Dominion EnergyShare partner, a crisis program of last resort that is not income-based (heating season Oct 1-May 31; cooling season June 1-Sept 30), with additional help available for people aged 60 and older, veterans and people with disabilities. EnergyShare recipients also qualify for a free home energy assessment and energy efficiency upgrades. The program additionally provides rent and mortgage assistance, as funding permits, to households with a 5-Day Pay-or-Quit or foreclosure notice. ACTS does not cover internet, cell phone, gasoline, medical bills or prescriptions.

services.description: Domestic Violence Services (Turning Points) operates an 18-bed confidential Safe House where survivors and their children may stay up to 45 days at no cost, with case management, help finding housing and employment, and children's case management. Also provides court advocacy and accompaniment, assistance applying for protective orders, crisis counseling, safety planning, 15-week psycho-educational support groups for adults, age-grouped children's programs (Littles, Mids, High-School), and groups for court-ordered men and women. Sexual Assault Services is the only sexual assault crisis center serving the Greater Prince William Area, supporting roughly 400 individuals and family members each year with hospital forensic exam accompaniment, criminal justice accompaniment, individual advocacy, and support groups including ongoing groups at the Prince William Adult Detention Center. All services are free and offered in English and Spanish.

records.notes: Contact OAR for a reentry intake or submit a Reentry and Family Services referral. Employment assistance is generally provided as part of an individualized case plan.

services.description: Provides employment assistance for justice-involved and formerly incarcerated individuals. Case managers help participants become employment-ready, identify job opportunities, and connect with local employers willing to consider applicants with criminal records. Reentry assistance may also address employment-related needs such as identification, transportation to interviews, work clothing, tools, training, and other barriers to obtaining or maintaining employment.

records.raw_hours_text: Mon-Fri 9am-5pm
records.raw_eligibility_text: Contact OAR for a reentry intake or submit a Reentry and Family Services referral. Employment assistance is generally provided as part of an individualized case plan.

records.notes: Contact OAR for assessment and case management. Financial assistance is needs-based and is not a general public cash-assistance program.

services.description: Provides limited direct financial and emergency assistance to eligible justice-involved individuals and their families as part of reentry and family services. Assistance may help with urgent needs related to housing stability, utilities, transportation, work expenses, food, clothing, identification, or other barriers that could interfere with successful reentry and family stability. Assistance depends on individual need and available resources.

records.raw_hours_text: Mon-Fri 9am-5pm
records.raw_eligibility_text: Contact OAR for assessment and case management. Financial assistance is needs-based and is not a general public cash-assistance program.

records.notes: Contact Community Services or visit participating recovery-support programs. Some peer and recovery services may be available without a formal external referral.

services.description: Provides peer-based recovery support for people affected by mental health and substance-use challenges. Peer specialists offer lived-experience-based encouragement, recovery navigation, connections to treatment and community resources, support groups, harm-reduction information, and other recovery-oriented services.

records.raw_hours_text: Varies by peer program, support group, and location.
records.raw_eligibility_text: Contact Community Services or visit participating recovery-support programs. Some peer and recovery services may be available without a formal external referral.

records.notes: Eligibility and referral requirements vary. Supported Employment serves individuals meeting program criteria who are referred through the Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services (DARS).

services.description: Provides vocational rehabilitation for eligible adults with serious mental illness, co-occurring disorders, or developmental disabilities. Programs include psychosocial rehabilitation and supported employment, helping participants identify employment interests, conduct job searches, build workplace skills, obtain competitive community employment, and receive ongoing support to maintain employment.

records.raw_hours_text: Varies by program and participant schedule.
records.raw_eligibility_text: Eligibility and referral requirements vary. Supported Employment serves individuals meeting program criteria who are referred through the Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services (DARS).

records.notes: No external referral is required to ask for help. Call Community Services or the MAT/recovery program directly. Current MAT information lists 703-792-2628 for assistance with opioid or alcohol recovery services.

services.description: Provides assessment and outpatient treatment for substance-use and co-occurring disorders, including individual and group counseling, case management, psychiatric services, Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT), peer recovery support, harm-reduction education, naloxone access, and referrals to detoxification or residential treatment when appropriate.

eligibility.details: No external referral is required to ask for help. Call Community Services or the MAT/recovery program directly. Current MAT information lists 703-792-2628 for assistance with opioid or alcohol recovery services.

records.raw_hours_text: Program and clinic schedules vary. MAT clinic services are offered at designated Manassas and Woodbridge locations; contact the program for current availability.

records.notes: Call 703-792-7800 in Manassas or 703-792-4900 in Woodbridge. The Crisis Receiving Center at 14011 Worth Ave, Woodbridge also accepts walk-ins 24/7.

services.description: Provides 24/7 behavioral-health crisis assessment, intervention, and screening for individuals experiencing mental health or substance-use crises, including assessment for psychiatric hospitalization when appropriate. Scheduled and walk-in crisis services are available through Community Services, and the Prince William Crisis Receiving Center provides 24/7 walk-in crisis care.

records.raw_hours_text: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Walk-in Community Services crisis services are available Monday–Thursday, 8:00 AM–8:00 PM and Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM; emergency staff remain available after hours, weekends, and holidays.
records.raw_eligibility_text: Call 703-792-7800 in Manassas or 703-792-4900 in Woodbridge. The Crisis Receiving Center at 14011 Worth Ave, Woodbridge also accepts walk-ins 24/7.
